question: For outpatients with seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis or urticaria, how do newer (second-generation) antihistamines compare with each other and with placebo or other treatments in effectiveness and harms?
eligibility: Adults or children with seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis, or with acute or chronic urticaria.
A newer (second-generation) antihistamine (for example cetirizine, desloratadine, fexofenadine or loratadine) compared with another antihistamine, placebo or another treatment.
Symptom or quality-of-life outcomes, or adverse events.
Randomized controlled trials; controlled observational studies for harms.
as_of_source: Day after latest Entrez date among included SYNERGY records (lower bound).
source: Cohen et al. 2006 screening collection, Antihistamines SYNERGY subset (16 included PubMed IDs): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asreview/systematic-review-datasets/metadata-v1-final/datasets/Cohen_2006/output/online/Antihistamines.csv; source paper DOI https://doi.org/10.1197/jamia.M1929
notes: Question and eligibility reconstructed from the Drug Effectiveness Review Project (Oregon EPC) drug-class review this subset came from, not from its original protocol. The Cohen 2006 collection drew citations from a 1994-2003 MEDLINE subset (TREC 2004 Genomics), so gold covers 1994-2003 only: recall is valid, but result counts include earlier literature. The answer key uses label_included PubMed IDs (article-level inclusion).
